payload.title: Add unevaluated status upstream of unplanned and wire the lifecycle
payload.description: New status unevaluated, upstream of unplanned. task add defaults new tasks here unless a status is given explicitly; a description edit resets a task to unevaluated. Transitions: unevaluated -> unplanned or unevaluated -> submitted (set by the evaluator). session status and task next must treat unevaluated as not-actionable and not render it as 'needs a plan'. Touches the canonical status lifecycle (ED-1529). Prerequisite for the evaluator job.

payload.title: Implement the description-sufficiency evaluator job
payload.description: The bespoke job that registers with the E-698 runner. For each unevaluated task, assembles the persisted-artifact context (description + parent + sibling titles + linked decisions — deliberately NOT the filing session's context) and calls a cheap model (claude -p) to judge description sufficiency, then sets status to submitted or unplanned and emits the transition as an event with evaluator attribution. Risk lean is a config knob defaulting toward submit. Runs as the belt (inline at file time when an agent does it) and suspenders (background sweep over the unevaluated queue).

payload.title: Add a per-task opt-out so the evaluator leaves a task alone
payload.description: Optional per-task flag/field marking a task as hands-off for the description-sufficiency evaluator (E-1844), for the rare 'AI, don't touch this one' case. The unevaluated status already handles the common exclusions (anything a human has moved is out of the queue by construction), so this is only the explicit exception. Deferred to maybe pending evidence it's needed.

fields.text:
# Author VISION.md

Write `VISION.md` at the repo root — a standalone narrative describing what we
envision Endless will be. Draw the substance from the analysis on this task.

- Prose narrative, not a table or bullet outline.
- Forward-looking: describe the envisioned end-state. No exists/planned split.
- Tell the arc (single-developer session management → a multi-developer
  substrate for AI-agent-driven work), then develop the tenets.
- Give the "lower human review burden" philosophy a prominent place.

Scope: this task authors `VISION.md` and nothing else.
fields.analysis:
## Source material for VISION.md

**The arc.** Endless began as a way for one developer to manage many concurrent
Claude Code sessions — first across terminal tabs, then across tmux windows. The
envisioned future is a substrate for many developers collaborating on the same
projects, each driving many AI-agent sessions.

**Core tenets to develop as narrative:**

1. **Humans managing ~2 orders of magnitude more concurrent work.** The human's
   job shifts from doing the work to steering many Claude Code sessions —
   research, coding, bug-fixing, and brainstorming.
2. **A task-centric loop.** The human has Claude Code file task(s), collaborates
   with it on a plan, then spawns each task into its own Claude Code session in a
   new tmux window with a task-specific git worktree and a config/DB sandbox. The
   session works the plan and hands back a verification script that gives the
   human confidence to land — merging the worktree back to `main`.
3. **Collaboration via git, not a server.** Several developers share one project
   by ordinary push/pull; each rebuilds their local view from the same committed
   history; no central authority; contributors never collide.
4. **The DB ledger as the foundation.** A JSONL write-ahead log is the source of
   record, with a rebuildable local DB and per-task isolation — behind-the-scenes
   plumbing that makes the collaboration above viable.

**Give headline billing to:** lowering the human's review burden. Agents report
in structured, skimmable form and don't make the human re-review what the tool
already computed. This is a core Endless philosophy and deserves a prominent place
in the narrative.

fields.title: Build a fire-once background job runner for Endless

payload.title: Build a long-running background daemon that fires the job runner on events and clock ticks
payload.description: The true general-purpose, long-running daemon. Fires the E-698 fire-once runner on events — including clock-tick events — so background jobs run without depending on a session monitor being live. Independent of tmux; the successor trigger to session-monitor ticks for machines/contexts where no monitor is running.

fields.title: Build the description-sufficiency evaluator that routes unevaluated tasks to unplanned or submitted
fields.description: The bespoke job that registers with the E-698 fire-once runner. For each unevaluated task it assembles the persisted-artifact context (description + parent + sibling titles + linked decisions — deliberately NOT the filing session's context) and calls a model via the shared run_internal_claude helper with a config-resolved model (standardize the config key so verb auto-registration and this evaluator resolve their model the same way; do not hardcode 'claude -p'). It then sets status to submitted (description is a sufficient spec) or unplanned (needs a planning session) and emits the transition as an event with evaluator attribution. submitted is one of two neutral outcomes, not the goal; no dependence on complexity/risk ratings. Runs as belt (inline at file time) and suspenders (background sweep over the unevaluated queue). Needs the unevaluated status (blocked by that task).

fields.text:
# README rework

Today README.md is largely a CLI reference (roughly the Project Management, Task Management, Documents, Web Dashboard, Hooks sections). Refocus it on onboarding a new human.

## Keep and lead with
- What Endless is — the elevator description (task tree, decisions as first-class artifacts, per-task worktrees, session tracking, optional enforcement, dashboard).
- Install — the install steps.
- Getting started — the minimal first-use path.

## Move out
- The exhaustive CLI reference and broad how-to-use material. Link to the docs guide index for deeper use.
- Note that the guide is written for a Claude Code session but humans still benefit from it.

## Link out to the contributor docs
- Link to `ROADMAP.md` (the exists/planned contributor roadmap) and `VISION.md` (the envisioned-end-state narrative). Keep the pointers short; do not inline their content — that bulks the README. (Folded in from a separate slim-README follow-up that this task supersedes.)

## Keep in sync
- The canonical status-lifecycle mermaid block is embedded byte-identical in README.md, CLAUDE.md, and docs guide index between the canonical markers; preserve that invariant (a verify script asserts they match).

fields.outcome: Superseded by E-1832 (Rewrite README). The one distinct requirement — link the refocused README to ROADMAP.md and VISION.md — was folded into E-1832's plan. Two tasks both rewriting README was redundant.

payload.title: Build a pluggable calling-harness layer for Endless internal LLM invocations
payload.description: Endless's internal model helper (run_internal_claude) is hardcoded to Claude — name and all. Introduce a pluggable calling-harness abstraction so internal evaluations (verb auto-registration, the E-1844 description-sufficiency evaluator, etc.) can invoke Claude, Codex, or other agent CLIs, with the harness + model selected via endless config. Optionally a direct API-key plugin if users ever demand it. Outbound counterpart to E-817 inbound hook-adaptor decoupling; together they make Endless agent-harness-agnostic in both directions.
